caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 760 of 1997
lawyer:
Nazmul Huda, Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Tofailur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondents.
parties:
Gold Coin Textile and Garments ------- Judgment debtor-Petitioner
Vs.
Gul Ahmed Jute Mills Ltd ------- Decree-holder Respondents
full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ: The respondent as plaintiff filed Other Suit No. 70 of 1987 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong for ejectment of the defendant-petitioner from the suit premises, realization of arrear rent and compensation for illegal occupation of the suit premises. The suit was decreed for eviction of the defendant-petitioner and also for recovery of Taka 32,18,132.00 from the defendant after adjusting Taka 7,03,156.00 which was already paid during the pendency of the suit. The defendant-petitioner was directed to pay the decretal amount (Taka 32,18,132 Taka 7,03,156 Taka 25,14,976.00) to the plaintiff and to vacate the suit premises within 60 days from the date of the judgment and decree dated 30-11-91, failing which the defendant was liable to pay compensation at the rate of Taka 2,000.00 per day. The plaintiff-respondent put the decree in execution on 9-3-92 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong being Other Execution Case No. 5 of 1992. 

 2. For the purpose of disposal of this leave petition it will be sufficient to notice that the learned Subordinate Judge passed an order on 14-3-95 in the execution proceeding requiring the defendant-judgment-debtor-petitioner to furnish a bank guarantee in favour of the plaintiff-decree-holder-respondent for an amount of Taka 12,82,000.00 before vacating the suit premises. This order was passed on the application of the petitioner for permission to vacate the suit premises. Being aggrieved by the said order the petitioner moved the High Court Division in revision but without any success. The Rule issued in the revision case No. 1896 of 1995 was discharged by a Division Bench by the impugned judgment and order dated 27 May, 1997. 

 3. Mr Nazmul Huda, learned Counsel for the petitioner, submits that both the learned Subordinate Judge and the High Court Division upon a mistaken view of an earlier order of the High Court Division wrongly held that the petitioner was required to furnish security for the alleged dues (as to compensation) of the decree-holder-respondent. He submits that there cannot be any obstruction caused to vacating the suit premises by the petitioner which it is required to do under the decree on pain of paying a daily compensation. The decree-holder has been illegally preventing the petitioner from vacating the suit premises for undue enrichment as the decree provides for a daily compensation of Taka 2,000.00 in case of failure to vacate. The petitioner not only satisfied the decretal amount but also paid about Taka 7,00,000.00 on account of compensation. Mr Huda submits that the learned Subordinate Judge illegally put the condition of a bank guarantee before vacating the suit premises. 

 6. It appears that the decree-holder came to the High Court Division in revision, Civil Revision No. 3440 of 1994, impugning certain orders of the executing Court. By judgment and order dated 30 January, 1995 the Rule was disposed of in that case with the observation as follows: 

 9. Is the judgment-debtor-petitioner at all required to furnish security before vacating the suit premises by reason of the order of the High Court Division as quoted above? It has been made very clear in the said order that the amount of security will be excluding the quantum of compensation; in other words, there will have to be no security for any amount of compensation which may be due. Therefore having regard to the facts which are practically admitted, namely, that the decretal dues have already been satisfied and the dues referred to in the application dated 8-9-94 relate to compensation, the order requiring the judgment-debtor to furnish bank guarantee before vacating the suit premises was not legal and proper. There is substance in the contention of the petitioner that the order passed by the High Court Division in the earlier revision case was misconstrued by the learned Subordinate Judge as also by the High Court Division.
